stimuli.title: Eight boxes labelled Deepa, Nisha, Kiran, Charu, Bina, Riya, Gita, Ovi are stacked one above another. Position 1 is at the bottom and position 8 at the top.
stimuli.body:
Use all the following clues:
• Kiran occupies position 2 from the bottom.
• Exactly 3 occupied positions separate Nisha and Gita in the stated order.
• Exactly 2 occupied positions separate Nisha and Charu in the stated order.
• Exactly 0 occupied positions separate Deepa and Ovi in the stated order.
• Exactly 2 occupied positions separate Nisha and Ovi in the stated order.
• Exactly 1 occupied positions separate Bina and Ovi in the stated order.
stimuli.solution: position 1 from the bottom: Charu; position 2 from the bottom: Kiran; position 3 from the bottom: Riya; position 4 from the bottom: Nisha; position 5 from the bottom: Bina; position 6 from the bottom: Deepa; position 7 from the bottom: Ovi; position 8 from the bottom: Gita

stimuli.title: Gita, Aditi, Farah, Kiran, Bina, Nisha, Esha, Isha occupy eight flats on floors 1 (bottom) to 4 (top). Each floor has Flat A to the west of Flat B. Each flat has one resident. For ordering only, count Floor 1 A, Floor 1 B, Floor 2 A, Floor 2 B, and so on.

• Esha occupies floor 2, flat B.
• Nisha and Isha live in the same flat letters.
• Gita and Kiran live in different flat letters.
• Farah and Esha live in different flat letters.
• The floor numbers of Kiran and Esha differ by 1.
• Gita lives below Kiran.
• The floor numbers of Kiran and Nisha differ by 2.
• Farah lives above Isha.
• Aditi lives below Esha.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few lockers are cheques. All cheques are accounts. No accounts is a bonds.
Conclusions:
I. Some lockers are not cheques.
II. No cheques is a bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some lockers are cheques. All cheques are accounts. No accounts is a bonds.
Conclusions:
I. Some lockers are accounts.
II. Some cheques are bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few lockers are cheques. Some cheques are accounts. All accounts are bonds.
Conclusions:
I. All lockers are bonds.
II. No cheques is a bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: No lockers is a cheques. Some cheques are accounts. All accounts are bonds.
Conclusions:
I. All lockers are bonds.
II. Some bonds are cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: S = T = P < U > X.
Conclusions: I. U < P   II. T ≤ X.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
Statements: V < Q = T > S < X.
Conclusions: I. Q ≥ S   II. X ≤ T.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
Statements: R < V > U < Q < X.
Conclusions: I. X > V   II. Q ≤ V.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Either I or II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. Together the alternatives cover every permissible ordering, so either I or II follows.

questions.stem:

Conclusions: I. Q < R   II. T > W.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
growth banking digital = su vo pa
growth rural savings = ka vo ni
banking rural access = pa ni ze
digital savings access = su ka ze
growth banking access = vo ze pa
What is the code for “savings”?
questions.explanation: Answer: ka. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: growth = vo, banking = pa, digital = su, rural = ni, savings = ka, access = ze.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 46 km east, turns left and walks 52 km, then turns left and walks 7 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 65. Net displacement is 39 km east and 52 km north. By Pythagoras, √(39² + 52²) = 65 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 26 km east, turns left and walks 32 km, then turns left and walks 2 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 40. Net displacement is 24 km east and 32 km north. By Pythagoras, √(24² + 32²) = 40 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 22 km east, turns left and walks 8 km, then turns left and walks 16 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 10. Net displacement is 6 km east and 8 km north. By Pythagoras, √(6² + 8²) = 10 km.

questions.stem: F is the mother of B. H is the son of B. A is the father of B. How is H related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. A is a parent of B, and H is B’s son. Hence H is A’s grandchild.

questions.stem: A is the brother of E. E is the mother of G. F is the father of A and E. How is A related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. A is the brother of G’s mother E. Therefore A is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: A is the only daughter of B. B is the father of A. D is the son of A. C is the sister of B. How is B related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. B is the father of A, and A is D’s mother. Thus B is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 59 candidates, a candidate is 21th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 36. New front rank = 21+3 = 24. Back rank = 59 − 24 + 1 = 36.

questions.stem: In a queue of 64 candidates, a candidate is 21th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 40. New front rank = 21+4 = 25. Back rank = 64 − 25 + 1 = 40.

In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.

access banking digital = mi vo ze

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 15 km east, turns left and walks 16 km, then turns left and walks 3 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 20. Net displacement is 12 km east and 16 km north. By Pythagoras, √(12² + 16²) = 20 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 18 km east, turns left and walks 12 km, then turns left and walks 9 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 15. Net displacement is 9 km east and 12 km north. By Pythagoras, √(9² + 12²) = 15 km.

questions.stem: H is the mother of B. F is the daughter of B. G is the father of B. How is F related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. G is a parent of B, and F is B’s daughter. Hence F is G’s grandchild.

questions.stem: H is the brother of C. C is the mother of E. B is the father of H and C. How is H related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. H is the brother of E’s mother C. Therefore H is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: E is the only daughter of C. C is the father of E. B is the son of E. F is the sister of C. How is C related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. C is the father of E, and E is B’s mother. Thus C is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 45 candidates, a candidate is 22th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 21. New front rank = 22+3 = 25. Back rank = 45 − 25 + 1 = 21.

questions.stem: In a queue of 51 candidates, a candidate is 22th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 26. New front rank = 22+4 = 26. Back rank = 51 − 26 + 1 = 26.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹1900 each. One earns 10% profit and the other incurs 25% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 4260.61. Recover each cost separately: 1900×100/110 + 1900×100/75. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 28 and 42 hours. An outlet empties it in 42 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank.
questions.explanation: Answer: 28. Net rate = 1/28 + 1/42 − 1/42 = 1/28. Take the reciprocal.

questions.stem: A boat covers 72 km in still water in 6 hours. If the stream flows at 3 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 3 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 27. Still-water speed = 12 km/h. Upstream speed = 12 − 3. Distance = speed × 3.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 9:6. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 7 months. A receives ₹259200 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?

questions.stem: A sum of ₹15000 earns ₹9000 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding?
questions.explanation: Answer: 21600. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 20%. Compound amount = 15000 × (1 + 20/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 170 litres of pure milk. 34 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)

questions.stem: The average weight of 29 people is 31 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 61. New total minus old total = (29+1)×(31+1) − 29×31 = 61.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 18 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 54. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+18)/(x+18) = 3/2 gives x = 18. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 200 m train moving at 57.6 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 14.4 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 16.67. Relative speed = (57.6 − 14.4) ×5/18 = 12 m/s. Time = 200/12.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 50%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹2100. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 47 km east, turns left and walks 48 km, then turns left and walks 11 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 60. Net displacement is 36 km east and 48 km north. By Pythagoras, √(36² + 48²) = 60 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 63 km east, turns left and walks 52 km, then turns left and walks 24 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 65. Net displacement is 39 km east and 52 km north. By Pythagoras, √(39² + 52²) = 65 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 51 km east, turns left and walks 40 km, then turns left and walks 21 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 50. Net displacement is 30 km east and 40 km north. By Pythagoras, √(30² + 40²) = 50 km.

questions.stem: D is the mother of F. A is the son of F. C is the father of F. How is A related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. C is a parent of F, and A is F’s son. Hence A is C’s grandchild.

questions.stem: C is the brother of H. H is the mother of F. E is the father of C and H. How is C related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. C is the brother of F’s mother H. Therefore C is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: E is the only daughter of F. F is the father of E. A is the son of E. C is the sister of F. How is F related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. F is the father of E, and E is A’s mother. Thus F is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 37 candidates, a candidate is 18th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 17. New front rank = 18+3 = 21. Back rank = 37 − 21 + 1 = 17.

questions.stem: In a queue of 52 candidates, a candidate is 20th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 29. New front rank = 20+4 = 24. Back rank = 52 − 24 + 1 = 29.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few files are deposits. All deposits are branches. No branches is a cheques.
Conclusions:
I. Some files are not deposits.
II. No deposits is a cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some files are deposits. All deposits are branches. No branches is a cheques.
Conclusions:
I. Some files are branches.
II. Some deposits are cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: No files is a deposits. Some deposits are branches. All branches are cheques.
Conclusions:
I. All files are cheques.
II. Some cheques are deposits.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few files are deposits. Some deposits are branches. All branches are cheques.
Conclusions:
I. All files are cheques.
II. No deposits is a cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 71 km east, turns left and walks 72 km, then turns left and walks 17 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 90. Net displacement is 54 km east and 72 km north. By Pythagoras, √(54² + 72²) = 90 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 22 km east, turns left and walks 16 km, then turns left and walks 10 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 20. Net displacement is 12 km east and 16 km north. By Pythagoras, √(12² + 16²) = 20 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 47 km east, turns left and walks 40 km, then turns left and walks 17 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?

questions.stem: E is the mother of B. A is the daughter of B. C is the father of B. How is A related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. C is a parent of B, and A is B’s daughter. Hence A is C’s grandchild.

questions.stem: E is the brother of B. B is the mother of D. A is the father of E and B. How is E related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. E is the brother of D’s mother B. Therefore E is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: F is the only daughter of E. E is the father of F. A is the son of F. D is the sister of E. How is E related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. E is the father of F, and F is A’s mother. Thus E is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 43 candidates, a candidate is 10th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 31. New front rank = 10+3 = 13. Back rank = 43 − 13 + 1 = 31.

questions.stem: In a queue of 39 candidates, a candidate is 14th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 22. New front rank = 14+4 = 18. Back rank = 39 − 18 + 1 = 22.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹2300 each. One earns 25% profit and the other incurs 10% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 4395.56. Recover each cost separately: 2300×100/125 + 2300×100/90. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 56 and 84 hours. An outlet empties it in 84 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank.
questions.explanation: Answer: 56. Net rate = 1/56 + 1/84 − 1/84 = 1/56. Take the reciprocal.

questions.stem: A boat covers 144 km in still water in 8 hours. If the stream flows at 5 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 4 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 52. Still-water speed = 18 km/h. Upstream speed = 18 − 5. Distance = speed × 4.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 8:7. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 5 months. A receives ₹115200 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?

questions.stem: A sum of ₹28000 earns ₹4200 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding?
questions.explanation: Answer: 30870. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 5%. Compound amount = 28000 × (1 + 5/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 80 litres of pure milk. 16 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)

questions.stem: The average weight of 17 people is 27 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 45. New total minus old total = (17+1)×(27+1) − 17×27 = 45.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 13 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 39. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+13)/(x+13) = 3/2 gives x = 13. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 130 m train moving at 57.6 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 7.2 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 9.29. Relative speed = (57.6 − 7.2) ×5/18 = 14 m/s. Time = 130/14.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 25%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹3300. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 20. New quantity / old quantity = 100/125. Reduction percentage = 25/125 ×100.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few deposits are bonds. Some bonds are accounts. All accounts are cards.
Conclusions:
I. All deposits are cards.
II. No bonds is a cards.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: No deposits is a bonds. Some bonds are accounts. All accounts are cards.
Conclusions:
I. All deposits are cards.
II. Some cards are bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some deposits are bonds. All bonds are accounts. No accounts is a cards.
Conclusions:
I. Some deposits are accounts.
II. Some bonds are cards.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few deposits are bonds. All bonds are accounts. No accounts is a cards.
Conclusions:
I. Some deposits are not bonds.
II. No bonds is a cards.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: V < P = W < X > Q.
Conclusions: I. Q ≤ X   II. X > V.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:

Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
rural savings digital = mi to ka
rural banking growth = pa ze ka
savings banking secure = ze ni to
digital growth secure = ni pa mi
rural savings secure = ni to ka
What is the code for “rural”?
questions.explanation: Answer: ka. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: rural = ka, savings = to, digital = mi, banking = ze, growth = pa, secure = ni.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 79 km east, turns left and walks 76 km, then turns left and walks 22 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 95. Net displacement is 57 km east and 76 km north. By Pythagoras, √(57² + 76²) = 95 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 36 km east, turns left and walks 40 km, then turns left and walks 6 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 50. Net displacement is 30 km east and 40 km north. By Pythagoras, √(30² + 40²) = 50 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 55 km east, turns left and walks 68 km, then turns left and walks 4 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 85. Net displacement is 51 km east and 68 km north. By Pythagoras, √(51² + 68²) = 85 km.

questions.stem: H is the mother of E. B is the son of E. G is the father of E. How is B related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. G is a parent of E, and B is E’s son. Hence B is G’s grandchild.

questions.stem: F is the brother of G. G is the mother of B. H is the father of F and G. How is F related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. F is the brother of B’s mother G. Therefore F is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: D is the only daughter of F. F is the father of D. A is the son of D. C is the sister of F. How is F related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. F is the father of D, and D is A’s mother. Thus F is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 64 candidates, a candidate is 10th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 52. New front rank = 10+3 = 13. Back rank = 64 − 13 + 1 = 52.

questions.stem: In a queue of 43 candidates, a candidate is 20th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 20. New front rank = 20+4 = 24. Back rank = 43 − 24 + 1 = 20.

questions.stem: An item costs ₹1400. It is marked above cost and sold at a 20% discount on marked price, earning 20% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 2100. Selling price = 1400 × 120/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.8 = 2100.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 32 days and B in 48 days. They work together for 4 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 25.33. Use 96 work units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2 units/day. Remaining = 96 − 4×5. Divide by A’s rate 3.

questions.stem: A vessel contains 65 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 13. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 13.

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 4 years, their combined age will be 104 years. Find the father’s present age.

In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
savings rural access = lu re su
savings banking credit = su ka mi
rural banking secure = lu vo ka
access credit secure = re mi vo
savings rural secure = vo lu su

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 65 km east, turns left and walks 68 km, then turns left and walks 14 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 85. Net displacement is 51 km east and 68 km north. By Pythagoras, √(51² + 68²) = 85 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 67 km east, turns left and walks 76 km, then turns left and walks 10 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 41 km east, turns left and walks 28 km, then turns left and walks 20 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?

questions.stem: A is the mother of H. B is the daughter of H. E is the father of H. How is B related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. E is a parent of H, and B is H’s daughter. Hence B is E’s grandchild.

questions.stem: E is the brother of H. H is the mother of C. G is the father of E and H. How is E related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. E is the brother of C’s mother H. Therefore E is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: G is the only daughter of H. H is the father of G. A is the son of G. E is the sister of H. How is H related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. H is the father of G, and G is A’s mother. Thus H is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 43 candidates, a candidate is 19th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 22. New front rank = 19+3 = 22. Back rank = 43 − 22 + 1 = 22.

questions.stem: In a queue of 62 candidates, a candidate is 17th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 42. New front rank = 17+4 = 21. Back rank = 62 − 21 + 1 = 42.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹3200 each. One earns 25% profit and the other incurs 10% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 6115.56. Recover each cost separately: 3200×100/125 + 3200×100/90. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 64 and 96 hours. An outlet empties it in 96 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank.
questions.explanation: Answer: 64. Net rate = 1/64 + 1/96 − 1/96 = 1/64. Take the reciprocal.

questions.stem: A boat covers 92 km in still water in 4 hours. If the stream flows at 5 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 2 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 36. Still-water speed = 23 km/h. Upstream speed = 23 − 5. Distance = speed × 2.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 5:3. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 4 months. A receives ₹96000 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?

questions.stem: A sum of ₹23000 earns ₹6900 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding?
questions.explanation: Answer: 27830. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 10%. Compound amount = 23000 × (1 + 10/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 140 litres of pure milk. 28 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 89.6. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 140 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The average weight of 29 people is 26 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 56. New total minus old total = (29+1)×(26+1) − 29×26 = 56.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 12 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 36. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+12)/(x+12) = 3/2 gives x = 12. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 220 m train moving at 72 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 7.2 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 12.22. Relative speed = (72 − 7.2) ×5/18 = 18 m/s. Time = 220/18.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 50%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹3000. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 33.33. New quantity / old quantity = 100/150. Reduction percentage = 50/150 ×100.

savings access rural = ka lu ze
banking digital rural = ka ni re

questions.stem: E is the mother of D. A is the son of D. B is the father of D. How is A related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. B is a parent of D, and A is D’s son. Hence A is B’s grandchild.

questions.stem: A is the brother of E. E is the mother of F. D is the father of A and E. How is A related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. A is the brother of F’s mother E. Therefore A is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: F is the only daughter of D. D is the father of F. C is the son of F. E is the sister of D. How is D related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. D is the father of F, and F is C’s mother. Thus D is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: An item costs ₹850. It is marked above cost and sold at a 10% discount on marked price, earning 12% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 16 days and B in 24 days. They work together for 4 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)

questions.stem: What is the difference (₹) between compound interest and simple interest on ₹17000 at 5% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)

questions.stem: A vessel contains 70 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 14. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 14.

questions.stem: The average of 20 numbers is 42. One number, 54, is replaced and the average rises by 7. What is the new number?

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 7 years, their combined age will be 78 years. Find the father’s present age.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
digital rural credit = re ze mi
digital secure growth = su ni re
rural secure access = mi ka ni
credit growth access = ka ze su

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 24 km east, turns left and walks 12 km, then turns left and walks 15 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 15. Net displacement is 9 km east and 12 km north. By Pythagoras, √(9² + 12²) = 15 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 62 km east, turns left and walks 76 km, then turns left and walks 5 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 39 km east, turns left and walks 20 km, then turns left and walks 24 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 25. Net displacement is 15 km east and 20 km north. By Pythagoras, √(15² + 20²) = 25 km.

questions.stem: H is the mother of D. F is the daughter of D. C is the father of D. How is F related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. C is a parent of D, and F is D’s daughter. Hence F is C’s grandchild.

questions.stem: D is the brother of G. G is the mother of E. A is the father of D and G. How is D related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. D is the brother of E’s mother G. Therefore D is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: G is the only daughter of E. E is the father of G. B is the son of G. D is the sister of E. How is E related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. E is the father of G, and G is B’s mother. Thus E is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 44 candidates, a candidate is 15th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 27. New front rank = 15+3 = 18. Back rank = 44 − 18 + 1 = 27.

questions.stem: In a queue of 47 candidates, a candidate is 18th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 26. New front rank = 18+4 = 22. Back rank = 47 − 22 + 1 = 26.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 9 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?

questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.explanation: Answer: 75. Net displacement is 45 km east and 60 km north. By Pythagoras, √(45² + 60²) = 75 km.

questions.stem: C is the mother of B. H is the son of B. E is the father of B. How is H related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. E is a parent of B, and H is B’s son. Hence H is E’s grandchild.

questions.stem: A is the brother of H. H is the mother of E. D is the father of A and H. How is A related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. A is the brother of E’s mother H. Therefore A is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: A is the only daughter of F. F is the father of A. H is the son of A. B is the sister of F. How is F related to H?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. F is the father of A, and A is H’s mother. Thus F is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 41 candidates, a candidate is 10th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?

growth access savings = pa su vo
growth banking digital = vo mi ni
access banking credit = pa ni to
savings digital credit = su to mi
growth access credit = to vo pa
What is the code for “credit”?
questions.explanation: Answer: to. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: growth = vo, access = pa, savings = su, banking = ni, digital = mi, credit = to.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 28 km east, turns left and walks 28 km, then turns left and walks 7 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 35. Net displacement is 21 km east and 28 km north. By Pythagoras, √(21² + 28²) = 35 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 28 km east, turns left and walks 32 km, then turns left and walks 4 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 40. Net displacement is 24 km east and 32 km north. By Pythagoras, √(24² + 32²) = 40 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 61 km east, turns left and walks 52 km, then turns left and walks 22 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 65. Net displacement is 39 km east and 52 km north. By Pythagoras, √(39² + 52²) = 65 km.

questions.stem: A is the mother of H. D is the daughter of H. G is the father of H. How is D related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. G is a parent of H, and D is H’s daughter. Hence D is G’s grandchild.

questions.stem: B is the brother of H. H is the mother of G. F is the father of B and H. How is B related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. B is the brother of G’s mother H. Therefore B is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: H is the only daughter of G. G is the father of H. E is the son of H. B is the sister of G. How is G related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. G is the father of H, and H is E’s mother. Thus G is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 55 candidates, a candidate is 18th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 35. New front rank = 18+3 = 21. Back rank = 55 − 21 + 1 = 35.

questions.stem: In a queue of 36 candidates, a candidate is 19th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 14. New front rank = 19+4 = 23. Back rank = 36 − 23 + 1 = 14.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹2800 each. One earns 10% profit and the other incurs 25% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 6278.79. Recover each cost separately: 2800×100/110 + 2800×100/75. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 66 and 99 hours. An outlet empties it in 99 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank.
questions.explanation: Answer: 66. Net rate = 1/66 + 1/99 − 1/99 = 1/66. Take the reciprocal.

questions.stem: A boat covers 168 km in still water in 8 hours. If the stream flows at 2 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 4 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 76. Still-water speed = 21 km/h. Upstream speed = 21 − 2. Distance = speed × 4.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 9:3. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 9 months. A receives ₹259200 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 324000. Profit ratio is 108:27. Each ratio unit = ₹2400. Total = 135 × 2400.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹15000 earns ₹2250 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 16537.5. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 5%. Compound amount = 15000 × (1 + 5/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 110 litres of pure milk. 22 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 70.4. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 110 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The average weight of 15 people is 43 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 59. New total minus old total = (15+1)×(43+1) − 15×43 = 59.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 14 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 42. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+14)/(x+14) = 3/2 gives x = 14. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 140 m train moving at 57.6 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 14.4 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 11.67. Relative speed = (57.6 − 14.4) ×5/18 = 12 m/s. Time = 140/12.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 20%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹1900. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 16.67. New quantity / old quantity = 100/120. Reduction percentage = 20/120 ×100.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 46 km east, turns left and walks 40 km, then turns left and walks 16 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 50. Net displacement is 30 km east and 40 km north. By Pythagoras, √(30² + 40²) = 50 km.

questions.stem: A is the mother of C. D is the son of C. F is the father of C. How is D related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. F is a parent of C, and D is C’s son. Hence D is F’s grandchild.

questions.stem: G is the brother of D. D is the mother of A. C is the father of G and D. How is G related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. G is the brother of A’s mother D. Therefore G is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: A is the only daughter of C. C is the father of A. D is the son of A. B is the sister of C. How is C related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. C is the father of A, and A is D’s mother. Thus C is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 60 candidates, a candidate is 17th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 41. New front rank = 17+3 = 20. Back rank = 60 − 20 + 1 = 41.

questions.stem: In a queue of 52 candidates, a candidate is 18th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 31. New front rank = 18+4 = 22. Back rank = 52 − 22 + 1 = 31.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
credit digital banking = pa ka su
credit rural savings = su ni vo
digital rural growth = pa ni ze
banking savings growth = ze vo ka
credit digital growth = ze pa su
What is the code for “credit”?
questions.explanation: Answer: su. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: credit = su, digital = pa, banking = ka, rural = ni, savings = vo, growth = ze.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 29 km east, turns left and walks 24 km, then turns left and walks 11 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 30. Net displacement is 18 km east and 24 km north. By Pythagoras, √(18² + 24²) = 30 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 60 km east, turns left and walks 64 km, then turns left and walks 12 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 80. Net displacement is 48 km east and 64 km north. By Pythagoras, √(48² + 64²) = 80 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 48 km east, turns left and walks 32 km, then turns left and walks 24 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 40. Net displacement is 24 km east and 32 km north. By Pythagoras, √(24² + 32²) = 40 km.

questions.stem: B is the mother of F. A is the daughter of F. C is the father of F. How is A related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. C is a parent of F, and A is F’s daughter. Hence A is C’s grandchild.

questions.stem: G is the brother of B. B is the mother of H. A is the father of G and B. How is G related to H?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. G is the brother of H’s mother B. Therefore G is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: B is the only daughter of A. A is the father of B. D is the son of B. H is the sister of A. How is A related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. A is the father of B, and B is D’s mother. Thus A is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 64 candidates, a candidate is 17th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 45. New front rank = 17+3 = 20. Back rank = 64 − 20 + 1 = 45.

questions.stem: In a queue of 55 candidates, a candidate is 21th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 31. New front rank = 21+4 = 25. Back rank = 55 − 25 + 1 = 31.

questions.stem: [Table set] A new branch F has a total equal to the average total at A and E. Its categories are split in ratio 2:3. What is the number in its second category?

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹2000 each. One earns 10% profit and the other incurs 25% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 4484.85. Recover each cost separately: 2000×100/110 + 2000×100/75. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 36 and 54 hours. An outlet empties it in 54 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank.
questions.explanation: Answer: 36. Net rate = 1/36 + 1/54 − 1/54 = 1/36. Take the reciprocal.

questions.stem: A boat covers 132 km in still water in 6 hours. If the stream flows at 4 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 3 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 54. Still-water speed = 22 km/h. Upstream speed = 22 − 4. Distance = speed × 3.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 4:9. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 9 months. A receives ₹129600 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 348300. Profit ratio is 48:81. Each ratio unit = ₹2700. Total = 129 × 2700.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹21000 earns ₹9450 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 27772.5. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 15%. Compound amount = 21000 × (1 + 15/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 130 litres of pure milk. 26 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 83.2. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 130 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The average weight of 15 people is 41 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 57. New total minus old total = (15+1)×(41+1) − 15×41 = 57.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 16 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 48. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+16)/(x+16) = 3/2 gives x = 16. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 210 m train moving at 57.6 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 10.8 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 16.15. Relative speed = (57.6 − 10.8) ×5/18 = 13 m/s. Time = 210/13.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 50%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹3100. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 33.33. New quantity / old quantity = 100/150. Reduction percentage = 50/150 ×100.

questions.stem: C is the mother of H. E is the son of H. B is the father of H. How is E related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. B is a parent of H, and E is H’s son. Hence E is B’s grandchild.

questions.stem: A is the brother of B. B is the mother of F. G is the father of A and B. How is A related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. A is the brother of F’s mother B. Therefore A is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: F is the only daughter of E. E is the father of F. A is the son of F. C is the sister of E. How is E related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. E is the father of F, and F is A’s mother. Thus E is the maternal grandfather.

In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
banking access rural = pa ni vo
banking savings secure = ze mi ni
access savings growth = vo mi su
rural secure growth = su ze pa
banking access growth = vo ni su

questions.stem: B is the mother of C. G is the daughter of C. E is the father of C. How is G related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. E is a parent of C, and G is C’s daughter. Hence G is E’s grandchild.

questions.stem: B is the brother of F. F is the mother of D. E is the father of B and F. How is B related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. B is the brother of D’s mother F. Therefore B is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: H is the only daughter of D. D is the father of H. B is the son of H. E is the sister of D. How is D related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. D is the father of H, and H is B’s mother. Thus D is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹27000 earns ₹16200 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding?

questions.stem: The average weight of 21 people is 50 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 19 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?

questions.stem: A 160 m train moving at 61.2 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 10.8 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 25%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹2300. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)

questions.explanation: Answer: 45. Net displacement is 27 km east and 36 km north. By Pythagoras, √(27² + 36²) = 45 km.

questions.stem: H is the mother of G. A is the son of G. F is the father of G. How is A related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. F is a parent of G, and A is G’s son. Hence A is F’s grandchild.

questions.stem: G is the brother of A. A is the mother of E. B is the father of G and A. How is G related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. G is the brother of E’s mother A. Therefore G is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: H is the only daughter of C. C is the father of H. B is the son of H. D is the sister of C. How is C related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. C is the father of H, and H is B’s mother. Thus C is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 60 candidates, a candidate is 16th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 42. New front rank = 16+3 = 19. Back rank = 60 − 19 + 1 = 42.

questions.stem: In a queue of 64 candidates, a candidate is 10th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 51. New front rank = 10+4 = 14. Back rank = 64 − 14 + 1 = 51.

questions.stem: A vessel contains 75 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 15. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 15.

questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:

I. All files are accounts.
II. No deposits is a accounts.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:

I. Some files are not deposits.
II. No deposits is a accounts.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:

Conclusions:
I. Some files are cheques.
II. Some deposits are accounts.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: P > Q < R = X > T.

Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Either I or II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. Together the alternatives cover every permissible ordering, so either I or II follows.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 24 km east, turns left and walks 28 km, then turns left and walks 3 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 35. Net displacement is 21 km east and 28 km north. By Pythagoras, √(21² + 28²) = 35 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 33 km east, turns left and walks 40 km, then turns left and walks 3 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 50. Net displacement is 30 km east and 40 km north. By Pythagoras, √(30² + 40²) = 50 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 57 km east, turns left and walks 44 km, then turns left and walks 24 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 55. Net displacement is 33 km east and 44 km north. By Pythagoras, √(33² + 44²) = 55 km.

questions.stem: B is the mother of D. E is the daughter of D. A is the father of D. How is E related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. A is a parent of D, and E is D’s daughter. Hence E is A’s grandchild.

questions.stem: C is the brother of D. D is the mother of F. B is the father of C and D. How is C related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. C is the brother of F’s mother D. Therefore C is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: F is the only daughter of D. D is the father of F. C is the son of F. G is the sister of D. How is D related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. D is the father of F, and F is C’s mother. Thus D is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 47 candidates, a candidate is 10th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 35. New front rank = 10+3 = 13. Back rank = 47 − 13 + 1 = 35.

questions.stem: In a queue of 41 candidates, a candidate is 9th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 29. New front rank = 9+4 = 13. Back rank = 41 − 13 + 1 = 29.

questions.explanation: Answer: 5830.3. Recover each cost separately: 2600×100/110 + 2600×100/75. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 62 and 93 hours. An outlet empties it in 93 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank.
questions.explanation: Answer: 62. Net rate = 1/62 + 1/93 − 1/93 = 1/62. Take the reciprocal.

questions.stem: A boat covers 144 km in still water in 8 hours. If the stream flows at 2 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 4 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 64. Still-water speed = 18 km/h. Upstream speed = 18 − 2. Distance = speed × 4.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 4:4. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 5 months. A receives ₹105600 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?

questions.stem: A sum of ₹28000 earns ₹12600 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding?
questions.explanation: Answer: 37030. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 15%. Compound amount = 28000 × (1 + 15/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 190 litres of pure milk. 38 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)

questions.stem: The average weight of 19 people is 36 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 56. New total minus old total = (19+1)×(36+1) − 19×36 = 56.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 17 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 51. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+17)/(x+17) = 3/2 gives x = 17. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 130 m train moving at 64.8 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 10.8 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 8.67. Relative speed = (64.8 − 10.8) ×5/18 = 15 m/s. Time = 130/15.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 20%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹2800. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 21 km east, turns left and walks 12 km, then turns left and walks 12 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 15. Net displacement is 9 km east and 12 km north. By Pythagoras, √(9² + 12²) = 15 km.

questions.stem: A is the mother of C. F is the son of C. B is the father of C. How is F related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. B is a parent of C, and F is C’s son. Hence F is B’s grandchild.

questions.stem: G is the brother of C. C is the mother of D. B is the father of G and C. How is G related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. G is the brother of D’s mother C. Therefore G is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: E is the only daughter of B. B is the father of E. C is the son of E. D is the sister of B. How is B related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. B is the father of E, and E is C’s mother. Thus B is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 55 candidates, a candidate is 10th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 43. New front rank = 10+3 = 13. Back rank = 55 − 13 + 1 = 43.

questions.stem: In a queue of 36 candidates, a candidate is 15th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 18. New front rank = 15+4 = 19. Back rank = 36 − 19 + 1 = 18.

Conclusions:
I. Some deposits are lockers.
II. Some bonds are accounts.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
rural secure credit = to pa su
rural access savings = pa ni vo
secure access banking = to vo re
credit savings banking = su ni re
rural secure banking = re to pa
What is the code for “credit”?
questions.explanation: Answer: su. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: rural = pa, secure = to, credit = su, access = vo, savings = ni, banking = re.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 67 km east, turns left and walks 72 km, then turns left and walks 13 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 90. Net displacement is 54 km east and 72 km north. By Pythagoras, √(54² + 72²) = 90 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 41 km east, turns left and walks 52 km, then turns left and walks 2 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 65. Net displacement is 39 km east and 52 km north. By Pythagoras, √(39² + 52²) = 65 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 48 km east, turns left and walks 52 km, then turns left and walks 9 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?

questions.stem: A is the mother of H. D is the daughter of H. C is the father of H. How is D related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. C is a parent of H, and D is H’s daughter. Hence D is C’s grandchild.

questions.stem: E is the brother of H. H is the mother of D. B is the father of E and H. How is E related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. E is the brother of D’s mother H. Therefore E is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: D is the only daughter of G. G is the father of D. C is the son of D. E is the sister of G. How is G related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. G is the father of D, and D is C’s mother. Thus G is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 44 candidates, a candidate is 8th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 34. New front rank = 8+3 = 11. Back rank = 44 − 11 + 1 = 34.

questions.stem: In a queue of 55 candidates, a candidate is 13th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 39. New front rank = 13+4 = 17. Back rank = 55 − 17 + 1 = 39.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹2800 each. One earns 25% profit and the other incurs 10% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 5351.11. Recover each cost separately: 2800×100/125 + 2800×100/90. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 22 and 33 hours. An outlet empties it in 33 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank.
questions.explanation: Answer: 22. Net rate = 1/22 + 1/33 − 1/33 = 1/22. Take the reciprocal.

questions.stem: A boat covers 96 km in still water in 8 hours. If the stream flows at 2 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 4 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 40. Still-water speed = 12 km/h. Upstream speed = 12 − 2. Distance = speed × 4.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 8:3. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 3 months. A receives ₹163200 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 178500. Profit ratio is 96:9. Each ratio unit = ₹1700. Total = 105 × 1700.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹19000 earns ₹2850 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 20947.5. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 5%. Compound amount = 19000 × (1 + 5/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 100 litres of pure milk. 20 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain?
questions.explanation: Answer: 64. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 100 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The average weight of 29 people is 25 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 55. New total minus old total = (29+1)×(25+1) − 29×25 = 55.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 10 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 30. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+10)/(x+10) = 3/2 gives x = 10. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 230 m train moving at 100.8 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 14.4 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 9.58. Relative speed = (100.8 − 14.4) ×5/18 = 24 m/s. Time = 230/24.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 50%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹3400. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 33.33. New quantity / old quantity = 100/150. Reduction percentage = 50/150 ×100.

questions.stem: D is the mother of F. C is the son of F. H is the father of F. How is C related to H?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. H is a parent of F, and C is F’s son. Hence C is H’s grandchild.

questions.stem: A is the brother of E. E is the mother of H. C is the father of A and E. How is A related to H?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. A is the brother of H’s mother E. Therefore A is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: E is the only daughter of D. D is the father of E. B is the son of E. H is the sister of D. How is D related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. D is the father of E, and E is B’s mother. Thus D is the maternal grandfather.

In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
digital access secure = re to vo
digital savings growth = ze re ka
access savings credit = ze vo mi
secure growth credit = ka to mi

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 70 km east, turns left and walks 76 km, then turns left and walks 13 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 95. Net displacement is 57 km east and 76 km north. By Pythagoras, √(57² + 76²) = 95 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 34 km east, turns left and walks 24 km, then turns left and walks 16 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?

questions.stem: G is the mother of E. F is the daughter of E. C is the father of E. How is F related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. C is a parent of E, and F is E’s daughter. Hence F is C’s grandchild.

questions.stem: A is the brother of E. E is the mother of D. B is the father of A and E. How is A related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. A is the brother of D’s mother E. Therefore A is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: H is the only daughter of E. E is the father of H. C is the son of H. B is the sister of E. How is E related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. E is the father of H, and H is C’s mother. Thus E is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 62 candidates, a candidate is 9th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 51. New front rank = 9+3 = 12. Back rank = 62 − 12 + 1 = 51.

questions.stem: In a queue of 46 candidates, a candidate is 15th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 28. New front rank = 15+4 = 19. Back rank = 46 − 19 + 1 = 28.

questions.stem: [Caselet set] A new branch F has a total equal to the average total at A and E. Its categories are split in ratio 2:3. What is the number in its second category?

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹1600 each. One earns 10% profit and the other incurs 10% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 3232.32. Recover each cost separately: 1600×100/110 + 1600×100/90. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 32 and 48 hours. An outlet empties it in 48 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank.
questions.explanation: Answer: 32. Net rate = 1/32 + 1/48 − 1/48 = 1/32. Take the reciprocal.

questions.stem: A boat covers 160 km in still water in 8 hours. If the stream flows at 5 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 4 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 60. Still-water speed = 20 km/h. Upstream speed = 20 − 5. Distance = speed × 4.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 4:6. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 5 months. A receives ₹57600 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 93600. Profit ratio is 48:30. Each ratio unit = ₹1200. Total = 78 × 1200.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹19000 earns ₹11400 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding?
questions.explanation: Answer: 27360. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 20%. Compound amount = 19000 × (1 + 20/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 160 litres of pure milk. 32 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 102.4. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 160 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The average weight of 28 people is 25 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 54. New total minus old total = (28+1)×(25+1) − 28×25 = 54.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 11 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 33. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+11)/(x+11) = 3/2 gives x = 11. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 250 m train moving at 64.8 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 10.8 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 16.67. Relative speed = (64.8 − 10.8) ×5/18 = 15 m/s. Time = 250/15.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 25%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹1900. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 20. New quantity / old quantity = 100/125. Reduction percentage = 25/125 ×100.
